ev.w_old_storyteller.text.E03: The young people at the gate refuse to believe that bread cost half as much in your youth, or that winters were real winters back then. You tell them anyway - and every time, the winters get colder.
ev.w_old_sun_bench.text.E03: A warm wall, the sun, a cup of watered wine and nothing to do until evening. You never knew a person could live like this.
ev.w_tomb_visit.text.E03: You brought wine, honey and flowers to the family tomb and read the names on the stone aloud, so the dead would know they are remembered.
ev.w_old_country_later.text.E03: You sit in the shade of a fig tree you planted yourself. The neighbors' children are convinced your figs are the best around, and they check regularly.
ev.w_child_quarrel.meet.success.E03: By the end of the meal you were pouring the in-laws' wine yourself.
ev.w_old_tomb.grand.ok.E03: The stone came out splendidly. You went to look at it three times, and each time you changed one word of the inscription.
ev.d_cold_house.divorce.ok.E03: The divorce took one day. You were surprised how few things turned out to be truly yours.
ev.d_cold_house.endure.ok.E03: You bring cakes to the temple and keep silent. The gods are patient - so must you be.
ev.d_temptation.text.E03: {g:The girl|The boy} you dreamed of in your youth has come back to town - widowed now, still laughing with {g:her|his} eyes alone. The meetings by the fountain grow longer, and at home {npc} asks why you're so late.
ev.d_temptation.farewell.ok.E03: You said goodbye at the same fountain. At home, {npc} wondered why you held {g=npc_sex:him|her} so tightly.
ev.d_affair_found.text.E03: {npc} found a note you should never have kept. There was only one question: 'How long?'
ev.d_jealous.temple.success.E03: The priest heard you both and told you to make a single offering together. On the way home you held hands for the first time in a month.
ev.d_jealous.temple.failure.E03: The priest talked at length, but {npc} only half listened and spent the whole way home glaring at passers-by.
ev.d_jealous_scene.text.E03: {npc} made a scene right in the middle of the market, in front of everyone - over a trivial chat with the fig seller. People laughed about it until evening.
ev.d_jealous_scene.endure.ok.E03: You silently picked up the spilled figs. But you take a different road to the market now.
ev.d_gambler.text.E03: The chest where you kept money for a rainy day is nearly empty. {npc} confesses: dice, a tavern debt - 'one more throw and I'd have won it all back.'
ev.d_gambler.pay.ok.E03: You paid off the tavern keeper. {npc} swears never again. You very much want to believe it.
ev.d_gambler.oath.E03: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} to the altar to swear an oath
ev.d_gambler.oath.success.E03: At the altar {npc} swore never to touch dice again - and seems to be keeping the oath.
ev.d_gambler.oath.failure.E03: The oath was sworn, the offering made. A month later you found the purse short again.
ev.d_gambler_again.text.E03: Two burly men from a gambling den stand in the doorway, holding an IOU. The name signed at the bottom: {npc}.
ev.d_gambler_again.pay.ok.E03: You counted out the coins without meeting anyone's eye. The chest is empty again.
ev.d_sp_illness.temple.E03: Pray and bring offerings to the temple
ev.d_sp_illness.temple.success.E03: Coming back from the temple, you heard a weak voice: {npc} was asking for water. The gods had listened.
ev.d_sp_illness.temple.failure.E03: This time the gods were silent. {npc} passed at dawn, holding your hand.
ev.d_grief_year.remember.ok.E03: Every month you bring wine and flowers to the tomb. Talking with the departed keeps you on your feet too.
ev.d_inlaws.gifts.ok.E03: Fine wine and an embroidered shawl did the trick: at the next feast they called you 'one of ours' for the first time.
ev.d_son_brawl.text.E03: Pounding on the door at night: {npc} has been taken by the watch {g=npc_sex:after a tavern brawl - the other man still can't get up|on a charge of stealing a bracelet from a market stall}. In the morning the case goes before the magistrate.
ev.d_son_brawl.lesson.ok.E03: You didn't go to the magistrate. Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} answer for what was done.
ev.d_son_released.away.ok.E03: Country air, hard work and not a tavern within a day's walk. We'll see.
ev.d_son_redeemed.text.E03: {npc} came to you with a first purse of honestly earned coins: 'This is for everything you did for me back then.' You didn't take a single coin - but you'll remember that day forever.
ev.d_son_criminal.text.E03: The watch is hunting a gang that's been robbing the harbor warehouses, and among the names given is {npc}. In the middle of the night, {g=npc_sex:he|she} is standing on your doorstep.
ev.d_elope.text.E03: {npc} ran off in the night {g=npc_sex:with a girl from the next street|with a young mule driver}, leaving only a note. The whole quarter is waiting to see what you'll do.
ev.d_elope.bring_back.success.E03: You caught up with the runaways at the second milestone. Everyone came home - and no one spoke.
ev.d_child_death.vow.E03: Make a vow to the gods
ev.d_child_death.vow.ok.E03: You brought a small clay figure to the temple and asked the gods to keep your little one safe where the living cannot go.
ev.d_illegit.text.E03: At dawn a basket with a baby was found at the gate, and a wax tablet: 'This child is yours. Remember that spring?' {npc} read the tablet before you did.
ev.d_illegit.take_in.ok.E03: You lifted the baby from the ground - by custom, that means acknowledging the child as yours. {npc} wouldn't look at you for a week.
ev.d_illegit.temple.E03: Take the child to the temple
ev.d_illegit.temple.ok.E03: The priests promised to find good people. You walked away without looking back - and you're still looking back.
ev.d_illegit.nurse.ok.E03: Every month you take a few coins to a wet nurse on the edge of town. {npc} pretends not to know where they go.
ev.d_drowning.funeral.ok.E03: You arranged everything properly: mourners, offerings, a coin for the ferryman. That's what friends do.
ev.d_drowning.family.ok.E03: You bring them grain and oil until the children grow up. You promised that at the funeral pyre.
ev.d_friend_sudden.text.E03: Only yesterday {npc} was joking with you at the baths, and today {g=npc_sex:he is|she is} gone. The heart, the physicians say. You never finished talking about something important.
ev.d_friend_sudden.eulogy.E03: Speak a farewell at the pyre
ev.d_friend_sudden.quiet.ok.E03: You came to the tomb at dawn, when no one else was there, and finished saying everything you hadn't had time to say.
ev.d_sib_accident.let_go.E03: Make an offering and let go
ev.d_sib_accident.let_go.ok.E03: You brought wine and honey to the gods below and asked them to be merciful.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.text.E03: You've learned that {npc} secretly sold the family house - without asking you, on a forged deed. The money, they say, is already spent.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.court.success.E03: The court ruled the deed a forgery, and you got your share back. There's no kinship between you anymore - only the verdict.
ev.d_sib_betrayal.court.failure.E03: The signature was ruled genuine. You lost both the house and the money spent on the case.
ev.d_sib_repays.text.E03: {npc} came with a heavy purse: 'This is for the house. I saved it coin by coin all these years.' For the first time in ages, you sat down at the table together.
ev.d_brother_war.work.failure.E03: The work didn't take. In the evenings {npc} goes to the tavern more and more and comes back at dawn.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.text.E03: A letter came from the harbor: the ship {npc} was sailing on has been taken by pirates. The ransom is five hundred coins by the end of summer, or the captives will be sold at a slave market somewhere across the sea.
ev.d_t_sib_captive.pay.ok.E03: You counted out the silver to the last coin. A month later {npc} stepped ashore - thin, sunburnt, but free.
ev.d_father_will.text.E03: After the funeral a young man from that second family came to you - with a will leaving him a third of everything. Now everyone will know your secret.
ev.d_father_will.contest.success.E03: The judges found the will improperly drawn. The young man got only a small share.
ev.d_t_secret_birth.text.E03: One night your mother {npc} confessed: you weren't born in this house. You were found as a baby on the temple steps and brought to a home that longed for a child. 'We loved you as our own. Forgive me for keeping silent.'
ev.d_t_secret_birth.seek.success.E03: An old priest remembered that winter and named a village. Someone with your face lives there - your blood kin. You sat in silence for a long time, studying each other.
ev.d_night_jail.text.E03: {g:An argument in a tavern turned into a brawl|A quarrel with a market woman turned into a scuffle}, and you spent the night in custody on the straw among thieves and drunks. In the morning the magistrate decides what to do with you.
ev.d_night_jail.argue.success.E03: Witnesses backed you up, and the magistrate let you go in peace.
ev.d_night_jail.argue.failure.E03: The magistrate didn't believe a word and doubled the fine - for insolence.
ev.d_t_theft.text.E03: A purse of silver has gone missing from your neighbor's house, and he's pointing at you: you were seen at his door that very evening. The watch is already leading you to the magistrate, and a crowd is gathering behind you.
ev.d_t_theft.witnesses.failure.E03: The witnesses contradicted each other. The magistrate ordered you to repay the loss twice over, and now a thief's reputation follows you.
ev.d_t_theft.flee.ok.E03: You left at night, taking only what you could carry. Now your name is on the list of fugitives.
ev.d_t_publican.text.E03: A tax farmer turned up with a scribe and a document: according to his records you've underpaid your taxes for three years, and with penalties it comes to three hundred coins. The records have clearly been doctored - but just try to prove it.
ev.d_t_publican.pay.ok.E03: You counted out the silver through gritted teeth. The tax farmer grunted with satisfaction - and marked you down as 'compliant.'
ev.d_t_publican.court.failure.E03: The judge dined with the tax farmer on feast days. You lost - and paid even more.
ev.d_t_publican.court.success.E03: You brought your receipts for all three years to court. The forgery came to light, and the tax farmer had to apologize.
ev.d_t_publican.bribe.success.E03: For a few coins the scribe 'found an error' in his own records. The debt vanished as suddenly as it had appeared.
ev.d_t_publican.neighbors.success.E03: Half the quarter came to the magistrate with identical complaints. The tax farmer was recalled, and now you're invited to every assembly.
ev.d_t_publican.neighbors.failure.E03: The neighbors nodded, but nobody went to the magistrate. You were left alone against the tax farmer - and he remembered.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.friends.success.E03: Friends chipped in, and a patron made up the rest. You walked free and swore to repay every coin.
ev.d_t_debt_prison.wait.success.E03: A month later the creditor, a superstitious old man, forgave the debt to fulfill a vow to the gods.
ev.d_chains.text.E03: The old case has run its course: you've been convicted and sent to hard labor - to the quarries, in chains, among thieves and runaway slaves.
ev.d_chains.intercede.ok.E03: Your friends reached the right people and spared no expense. The sentence was commuted to a fine - ruinous, but without chains.
ev.d_m_grave.text.E03: You brought wine and honey to the tomb by the road and told of everything that had happened that year. The wind rustled the grass - as if someone were listening.
ev.d_m_toy.text.E03: Sorting through a chest, you found a little clay horse with a chipped ear. You held it in your palms a long time, then set it on the shelf - in the most visible spot.
ev.v_wine_symposium.text.E03: At the banquet the master of the drinking ordered the wine served unmixed - 'the Scythian way.' Anyone who reaches for the water jug gets laughed at, and the cup goes round faster and faster.
ev.v_wine_symposium.neat.E03: Drink it neat like everyone else
ev.v_wine_symposium.mixed.E03: Mix it with water, as the elders did
ev.v_wine_grief.friend.ok.E03: You sat up until dawn, and more words were spent than wine. It helped.
ev.v_wine_grief.temple.E03: Go to the temple instead of the tavern
ev.v_wine_grief.temple.ok.E03: The temple is cool and smells of incense. You stayed until dark and walked home sober.
ev.v_wine_scandal.laugh.E03: Laugh it off: that was the wine talking
ev.v_wine_scandal.vow.E03: Swear never to drink unmixed wine again
ev.v_wine_fall.poppy.E03: Ask the physician for poppy juice against the pain
ev.v_wine_fall.poppy.ok.E03: The poppy juice eased the pain within the hour. The pain went; the sweet lightness stayed - and you remembered it.
ev.v_wine_fall.endure.E03: Grit your teeth and wash the pain down with wine
ev.v_wine_fall.endure.ok.E03: The wine dulled the pain, but the arm healed crooked. Now it aches whenever rain is coming.
ev.v_wine_quit.regimen.success.E03: The physician laid it all out: barley gruel, water, long walks, baths and sleep. The first month was torment, but you held on.
ev.v_wine_quit.regimen.failure.E03: For two weeks you dutifully drank barley gruel. In the third you slipped - and were too ashamed to go back to the physician.
ev.v_wine_quit.vow.E03: Make a vow to the gods
ev.v_wine_quit.vow.success.E03: You made your vow at the altar and left an empty jug in the temple. When the craving comes, you remember whom you promised.
ev.v_wine_quit.vow.failure.E03: You broke the vow at the very next festival. Now the craving comes mixed with fear of the gods.
ev.v_wine_quit.friend.success.E03: Your friend followed you like a shadow: steered you out of banquets, sat with you in the evenings. Within six months you stopped dreaming of wine.
ev.v_wine_relapse.text.E03: At the neighbours' wedding someone holds out a cup of neat wine: 'To the newlyweds! One won't hurt.' Everyone is watching.
ev.v_wine_sober.text.E03: A whole year without neat wine. Mornings are mornings again: a clear head, steady hands and money that no longer drains away into the tavern.
ev.v_wine_liver.text.E03: The whites of your eyes have turned yellow, your belly is swollen, and in the mornings the nausea keeps you in bed. The physician pressed your side for a long time and finally said it plainly: it's the wine.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.success.E03: Fear proved stronger than the craving. The yellow took months to fade, but you never touched unmixed wine again.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.failure.E03: You lasted a week. Your body called for wine louder than the physician's warnings.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.text.E03: {npc} set an empty jug down in front of you: 'It's the wine or me. I'm tired of scrubbing away your shame.'
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.temple.E03: Go to the temple together and make a vow
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.temple.failur: The vow was broken within a month. {npc} no longer goes anywhere with you - not to the temple, not to friends.
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.talk.success.E03: You talked half the night. For the sake of those eyes you poured the wine into the gutter - and never bought more.
ev.v_dice_first.small.success.E03: The knucklebones fell in the luckiest throw - all four showing different sides - and you left with a full purse. That night you dreamed of rattling dice.
ev.v_dice_first.big.success.E03: Luck followed you all evening. You raked in a pile of coins and realised nothing in the world fires the blood like this.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.text.E03: Tonight the dice seem to obey your hand: throw after throw, and the pile of coins in front of you keeps growing. The others scowl and demand one more round.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.double.success.E03: Luck held: you cleaned out the table to the last coin. The others left cursing - and they'll remember you.
ev.v_dice_loss.borrow.ok.E03: The moneylender counted out the coins without blinking. He named the interest as casually as if he were discussing the weather.
ev.v_dice_loss.refuse.success.E03: You raised a cry about a die with lead inside, and the winner, wanting no fuss, backed off. But the gambling dens don't welcome you any more.
ev.v_dice_quit.oath.E03: Swear an oath at the altar
ev.v_dice_quit.oath.success.E03: You swore by the gods and threw your dice into the temple fire. The oath holds tighter than any lock.
ev.v_dice_quit.oath.failure.E03: You broke the oath within a month and now avoid even looking at the temple.
ev.v_dice_quit.purse.success.E03: Now every coin is accounted for, and asking for gambling money is too shameful. A year later you noticed the rattle of dice had left your dreams.
ev.v_poppy_pain.text.E03: An old pain in your lower back has kept you awake for months. The physician takes out a vial of thick, dark poppy juice: 'Five drops in wine at night. No more - it's treacherous.'
ev.v_poppy_pain.endure.E03: Endure it: poppy makes people dull
ev.v_poppy_pain.baths.E03: Treat it with baths and rubdowns
ev.v_poppy_more.physician.failure.E03: The physician warned you, but the shop next door sells poppy juice with no advice at all.
ev.v_poppy_dreams.text.1.E03: Poppy dreams - slow, warm, golden. You woke toward evening and couldn't remember at first what day it was.
ev.v_poppy_cost.text.E03: The drug-seller has doubled the price of poppy juice: 'The ships from Egypt are late.' You don't have the money, and without the juice your whole body aches by evening.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.quit.success.E03: Fear of death proved stronger than the poppy. You smashed the vial on the stones and got through the withdrawal with clenched teeth.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary.E03: Go to the sanctuary of the healing god
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary.success.E0: You spent several nights in the sanctuary, and in a dream the god touched your forehead. In the morning the craving was weaker, and it weakened more each day.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary.failure.E0: The dreams in the sanctuary were as poppy-soaked as the ones at home. The god kept silent.
ev.v_poppy_quit.text.E03: A physician trained in the books of Hippocrates offers to wean you off the poppy: fewer drops each week, baths, barley gruel, walks. He warns you honestly: it will hurt, more than once.
ev.v_poppy_quit.refuse.E03: Refuse: without the poppy life is too grey
ev.v_poppy_relapse.text.E03: The old injury is aching again with the rains. And in the chest, wrapped in a rag, lies a forgotten vial with the last of the poppy juice.
ev.v_poppy_relapse.pour.ok.E03: You flung the juice into the hearth, and it hissed on the coals. The pain stayed, but the choice was yours.
ev.v_glut_feast.text.E03: The host is sparing nothing: eels, fat tuna, roast boar, mountains of honey cakes. You were full long ago, and still the dishes keep coming.
ev.v_glut_feast.napkin.E03: Wrap some treats in your napkin to take home
ev.v_glut_feast.napkin.ok.E03: Plenty of guests do it: treats in a napkin are fair spoils. At home you were greeted like a hero.
ev.v_glut_gout.diet.success.E03: Barley porridge, vegetables and water instead of banquets. Six months later your foot fit into a sandal again.
ev.v_glut_gout.poppy.E03: Dull the pain with poppy juice
ev.v_glut_gout.poppy.ok.E03: Poppy juice takes the pain away within the hour. It doesn't cure the gout - but you'd rather not think about that.
ev.v_greed_famine.usury.ok.E03: The neighbours took the grain and signed the notes. In spring you'll get yours back with plenty extra - and their quiet hatred thrown in.
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet.E03: Recite the whole alphabet to yourself, as the philosophers advise
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet.success.E03: Alpha, beta, gamma… by omega the anger was gone. Turns out the philosophers know a thing or two.
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet.failure.E03: You got as far as epsilon and blew up again. Letters are no match for rage.
ev.v_theft_chance.text.E03: The one you work for left you in charge of the takings and went away for a week. The coins lie in the chest, nobody has counted them, and payday is a long way off. You've also noticed your workmate already dipping into it.
ev.v_theft_chance.honest.ok.E03: The owner counted every last coin and was pleased. Trust is capital too.
ev.v_theft_caught.text.E03: Your employer went over several years of records, and the shortfall is too large to blame on mice. He is looking straight at you.
ev.v_theft_caught.confess.ok.E03: You returned every last coin, and it never came to court. But such things aren't forgotten: the sideways looks lingered for years.
ev.v_theft_caught.deny.failure.E03: Witnesses and records turned up. You had to repay double, and word of your sticky fingers spread through the whole quarter.
ev.v_vanity_purple.text.E03: The cloth merchant has a cloak dyed with genuine Tyrian purple. It costs as much as a craftsman earns in a year, but in it you'd look like someone people envy.
ev.v_lust_affair.yes.ok.E03: It was like a gulp of unmixed wine: sweet, heady and unsettling. You came home late, with an excuse made up on the way.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.curse.E03: Commission a curse on a lead tablet
ev.v_envy_neighbor.curse.ok.E03: The sorcerer scratched your neighbour's name on a lead tablet, rolled it up and dropped it down a well. You felt better - though the neighbour doesn't seem to have noticed.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.text.E03: {npc} pours neat wine before sunset more and more often, and the jars in the storeroom empty faster than you can buy new ones.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.talk.success.E03: You talked into the night. It turned out the wine was hiding a sadness you hadn't known about. The jars empty more slowly now.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.talk.failure.E03: {npc} took offence and shut down. There's no less wine in the house.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.hide.E03: Hide the wine and water it down in secret
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.hide.ok.E03: You started cutting the wine three to one. Time will tell whether the trick works.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician.E0: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} to a physician and the temple, whatever it costs
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician.su: Months of regimen, vows and sleepless nights. One day {npc} poured the wine into the gutter unprompted - and you wept with relief.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician.fa: The physician tried, the priests prayed, but within a month it was all back. The money is gone, and there's less hope left.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_end.text.E03: In winter {npc} took to bed and never rose again: the liver, the physician said, had been failing for a long time. The wine that promised relief took everything. The house is quiet, and you can't tell whether grief or guilt weighs on you more.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_moment.text.2.E03: At dinner {npc} drained a third cup of neat wine and launched into a song. You finished your meal alone in the courtyard.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.text.E03: {npc} keeps disappearing to the cockfights, coming home sometimes with a handful of coins, sometimes empty-handed with shifty eyes. Yesterday the tax money vanished from the chest.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.condition.fa: You cleared the debt, but the ban held only until the next races. It's all happening again.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.text.E03: A moneylender came to you with a note: {npc} borrowed against your house. It's due by the end of the month.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.divorce.ok.E: You renounced both the marriage and someone else's notes. The house was saved; the family wasn't.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.talk.E03: Explain how decent people drink: with water and in moderation
ev.v_rel_child_wine.talk.success.E03: {npc} nodded, wincing from the headache. You never saw neat wine in {g=npc_sex:his|her} cup again.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.text.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} is at the door - puffy-faced, in someone else's cloak, reeking of wine. {g=npc_sex:He|She} asks for a little money, 'just until tomorrow.'
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.give.ok.E03: 'Until tomorrow' stretched into forever. You knew it as you handed over the coins.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.takein.E03: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} in and keep the wine away
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.takein.success.E0: For a month {npc} raged, cursed and wept. And then one morning asked not for wine, but for work.
ev.v_rel_father_old.title.E03: The Old Man and the Wine
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.text.E03: {npc} has taken poppy juice for her aching joints for years, and now she takes it with no pain at all. She dozes through the day, and by evening she is searching for the vial with shaking hands.
The physician left, and {npc} was only angry: 'It's medicine, not wine.' The drops stayed.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.text.E03: {npc} barely gets up any more, doesn't recognise the neighbours and calls you by someone else's name. The physician is blunt: her heart can't take the poppy, but without it she will be in great pain.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.wean.failure.E: Her heart could bear neither the poppy nor its loss. {npc} slipped away quietly in her sleep, holding your hand.
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.text.E03: {npc}, your old friend, has lost at dice and asks you to stand surety for {g=npc_sex:him|her} with a moneylender: 'I'll pay it all back in six months, by the gods!'
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.vouch.success.E03: {npc} really did pay it all back - on time, to the last coin. The friendship passed the test of silver.
ev.t_road_robbers.text.E03: On an empty stretch of road five men step out of the bushes with clubs and knives. One grabs your mule's bridle, another is already rummaging through your packs. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.hand_over.ok.E03: They took your purse, your cloak, even your sandals. You limped home barefoot, counting every stone and every lost coin.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.success.E03: You grabbed a cart pole and knocked the first one flat. The rest scattered, but the leader looked back as he ran and memorized your face. You memorized his.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.failure.E03: There were too many. You woke in a ditch with a cracked head and no money - and, for some reason, the mule.
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff.success.E03: You waved so confidently at the dust beyond the bend that the robbers exchanged looks and melted into the brush. The dust turned out to be a flock of sheep.
ev.t_robbers_caught.text.E03: The robbers from the road have been caught. You're summoned to identify them and reclaim what's left of the loot. Among the bound men is a boy of thirteen who held your mule that day. He looks at you and says nothing.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.success.E03: You caught up with them in an alley: the chest is heavy and thieves aren't athletes. They dropped it and fled with only a handful of coins.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.failure.E03: In the dark you tripped over a barrel and smashed your knee. The footsteps faded, and with them everything you'd saved.
ev.t_night_burglary.curse.ok.E03: A wise woman scratched it onto a lead tablet - “May whoever took it neither sleep nor eat until it is returned” - and dropped it down a well. It hasn't brought the money back, but you sleep better.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.E03: You patched the wall and decided: from now on your money stays in a temple, under the eyes of gods and priests. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_burglar_returns.text.E03: In the morning there was a pouch of coins on your doorstep and a note in a clumsy hand: “Lift the curse. I can't take any more.” The tablet in the well did its work.
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.E03: Pray to the gods and make a vow
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.failure.E03: The gods heard, but took their time: you drifted two days on a broken spar. You survived - battered, with a vow on your heart.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.text.E03: You dreamed of the sea again, and a voice reminded you: you promised an offering for your rescue. At the temple the priest nodded as if he'd been expecting you. “The gods are patient, but they have long memories.”
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.pay.ok.E03: You ordered a little silver ship and a sacrifice for the whole quarter. It felt like shedding a sodden cloak.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.tablet.ok.E03: The tablet shows a sinking ship and you clinging to a spar. Modest but honest - the temple has hundreds like it.
ev.t_buried_treasure.text.E03: The plow clanks against something hard. Under the clods is a clay pot full of heavy old coins, green with age. Someone buried them during a long-ago war and never came back. Across the boundary stone, your neighbor is watching.
ev.t_buried_treasure.temple.ok.E03: The priests accepted the gift gratefully and set aside a small share for you. The earth gave the gods what wasn't hers - so the village says.
ev.t_buried_treasure.share.ok.E03: You divided the coins right there on the boundary. Now you have money - and someone who keeps the same secret.
ev.t_treasure_informer.text.E03: Someone has informed on you about the treasure. An official arrives with a scribe and guards. “Concealing a find is a crime. Where are the coins?”
ev.t_distant_inheritance.text.E03: A messenger brings a sealed letter: in a distant city a distant relative of yours has died childless - a man you never met. His will leaves everything to you: house, workshop, slaves. And debts, which no one can put a number to.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.text.E03: A distant cousin of the deceased has turned up with another will - supposedly a later one. The seals look suspiciously fresh, and the witnesses suspiciously well fed.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.court.success.E: The judge noticed the wax on the seals still smelled of the beehive. The forgery was thrown out; the inheritance is yours.
ev.t_friend_betrays.text.E03: You stood surety for {npc} when {g=npc_sex:he|she} needed a large loan. Now {npc} has vanished with the money, and the lender is at your door with a contract where your name is written right beside {g=npc_sex:his|hers}.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.success.E03: You found the runaway at the quay, luggage already on the gangplank. Nearly all the money came back. The friendship didn't.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.failure.E03: The ship left an hour before you arrived. The journey cost plenty, and the debt is still yours.
ev.t_friend_returns.text.E03: The one you stood surety for has come back - gray-haired, in an expensive cloak. He stands at your door holding a purse and can't raise his eyes. “I made my fortune overseas. Here's everything I owe you, and more.”
ev.t_friend_returns.take.ok.E03: You counted the coins in front of him. Every one. The debt is closed - and nothing more.
ev.t_friend_returns.forgive.ok.E03: You sat until morning over wine, remembering your youth. Not every friendship can be saved, but this one was.
ev.t_friend_returns.drive_away.ok.E03: You shut the door without taking a single coin. Pride is capital too.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead.success.E03: Your master remembered your years of service and sold a mule instead. You stay - for now.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.show_skill.ok.E03: You read the goods list aloud and tallied it in your head. The steward of a rich household, who'd come for a cook, outbid the contractor - and took you to the city instead of the mines.
ev.t_slave_born_free.search_family.ok.E0: You begged a mule driver to carry the old woman's words to the next town. Now all you can do is wait.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.refuse.ok.E03: You won't buy freedom at the price of yourself. The master scowls, the potter waits, and you save every coin on your own.
ev.t_master_heirs.court.success.E03: Your husband came to court himself and said he chose you of his own free will. The suit was dismissed and your share set down in writing.
ev.t_poetess.publish.success.E03: Your verses are copied onto papyrus and learned by heart. The best houses invite you, and even your family is proud now - out loud.
ev.t_poetess.burn.ok.E03: The hearth fire made short work of the papyrus. The lines still sound in your head, but soon they'll fade too.
ev.t_poems_live_on.text.E03: In a distant port you heard sailors you'd never met singing your verses - with mistakes, in their own way, but yours. None of them knows who wrote them. And somehow that's the most beautiful part.
ev.t_youth_teacher.text.E03: A wandering teacher - gray-haired, in worn sandals, with a bag of scrolls - watched you argue with a merchant and invited you to come with him: to study, copy books, see the world. But your hands are needed at home, and your father has no love for philosophers.
ev.t_youth_teacher.run_off.ok.E03: You caught up with the teacher at the city gate. Ahead: scrolls, arguments and new cities. Behind: a home where you won't soon be forgiven.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.text.E03: Your old teacher has died and left you everything he had: a chest of scrolls, a threadbare cloak, and a dozen pupils who are now looking at you.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.open_school.ok.E03: You hung a sign over the door and started teaching. The pay is small, but boys from the neighboring quarters come to you and no one else.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.sell_library.ok.E03: A book collector paid good money for the scrolls. The teacher would probably have winced - or perhaps laughed.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.donate.E03: Give the scrolls to a temple library
ev.t_plunder_share.spare.ok.E03: You led them through a breach in the wall to an olive grove. The woman pressed a ring into your hand and said something in her own language. The boy watched you go for a long time.
ev.t_plunder_share.loot_temple.ok.E03: You carried a golden bowl and a fistful of coins out of the temple. Wealth for life. They say foreign gods have long memories too.
ev.t_loot_curse.text.E03: Ever since you carried gold out of that temple, you dream of a burning hill. Misfortune follows misfortune, and the soothsayer put it bluntly: “The gods of that city want what is theirs.”
ev.t_loot_curse.sacrifice.ok.E03: You made sacrifices and hung up amulets. It's a little easier - or so it seems.
ev.t_grain_hoard.text.E03: The harvest failed, the grain ships are late, and the price of bread has tripled. And your granaries are full. At the gate stand both speculators with fat purses and the hungry with empty baskets.
ev.t_honorary_decree.text.E03: The city council has voted in your honor: to carve the decree in stone, set up your statue by the temple, and give you a seat of honor at festivals. Beneath the statue is an inscription about that hungry year.
ev.t_adoption.accept.ok.E03: The rite is done, the name changed. You have a house with columns, slaves and fields. Your own father, when he heard, said nothing - he simply turned away.
ev.t_uncover_crime.blackmail.ok.E03: Now once a month he silently slips you a pouch of coins. You both know it won't last forever.
